Adversarially verify this M13 finding. Read the real code (git diff main...HEAD + the file) and try to REFUTE it. Default isReal=false if false positive / pre-existing / out of scope / already handled.
Lens:correctness Sev:high
File:app/(admin)/admin/actions.ts (setUserSuspended, the `if (target.role === "provider")` block (~lines 110-116))
Reinstating a provider unconditionally sets provider status to 'approved', bypassing the approval/background-check gate
`setUserSuspended` flips provider status with `status: suspended ? "suspended" : "approved"`. The provider_status enum has four values: 'pending', 'approved', 'rejected', 'suspended'. The action treats suspension as a simple approved⇄suspended toggle, but the target provider may currently be 'pending' or 'rejected'. Two concrete defects introduced by this diff:
1. Suspending a 'pending' or 'rejected' provider overwrites their real status with 'suspended', destroying the original state (no record of what it was).
2. Reinstating then sets status to 'approved' regardless of the pre-suspension state — silently auto-approving a provider who was never approved (e.g. one who hasn't cleared the background check, or was explicitly 'rejected'). This bypasses the M3 approval gate and is safety-relevant for a marketplace whose providers are vetted.
This is fully reachable from the UI: components/admin/UsersTable.tsx renders a Suspend button for every non-admin row (including pending/rejected providers), and components/admin/ReportCard.tsx's 'Suspend target' calls the same action.
Suggestion:Don't infer the reinstated status. Read the provider's status before suspending and, on suspend, only move 'approved' providers to 'suspended' (leave 'pending'/'rejected' as-is, or store the prior status). On reinstate, restore the saved prior status (or only un-suspend providers whose current status is 'suspended', mapping back to 'approved' only when they were approved before). Alternatively, gate the provider-status write on `target` provider status === 'approved'/'suspended' so pending/rejected providers are never auto-approved.

=== m13 migration ===
-- =====================================================================
-- M13 — admin dashboard support: user suspension + a profiles column guard
-- that also closes a privilege-escalation hole (a user could previously PATCH
-- their own profiles.role to 'admin' via the owner-scoped RLS update policy).
-- =====================================================================

alter table public.profiles
  add column is_suspended boolean not null default false;

-- Freeze privileged profile columns for ordinary authenticated users. Trusted
-- server writes (service role → auth.uid() is null) and admins pass through.
create or replace function public.guard_profile_privileged_columns()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = public
as $$
begin
  if auth.uid() is null or public.is_admin() then
    return new;
  end if;
  -- A user editing their own profile cannot change their role or un-suspend
  -- themselves.
  new.role         := old.role;
  new.is_suspended := old.is_suspended;
  return new;
end;
$$;

create trigger profiles_guard_privileged
  before update on public.profiles
  for each row execute function public.guard_profile_privileged_columns();

-- Suspended customers can't be active. Exclude them from the "active customers"
-- strategic metric.
create or replace view public.admin_metrics_strategic as
select
  coalesce((select sum(total_price_cents) from public.sessions where status = 'completed'), 0)::bigint as gmv_cents,
  coalesce((select sum(commission_cents) from public.sessions where status = 'completed'), 0)::bigint as revenue_cents,
  coalesce((select sum(provider_earnings_cents) from public.sessions where status = 'completed'), 0)::bigint as provider_earnings_cents,
  (select count(*) from public.providers where status = 'approved')::int as active_providers,
  (select count(distinct b.customer_id)
     from public.bookings b
     join public.profiles p on p.id = b.customer_id
    where p.is_suspended = false)::int as active_customers,
  coalesce((select round(avg(rating)::numeric, 2) from public.reviews), 0)::numeric as avg_rating;

revoke all on public.admin_metrics_strategic from anon, authenticated;

I have fully verified the finding through every refutation angle. Let me record my conclusion.

Verification summary:

- **Enum confirmed**: `provider_status` has four values (`pending`, `approved`, `rejected`, `suspended`) — `lib/supabase/database.types.ts:639`. The action treats it as a binary `approved ⇄ suspended` toggle.
- **Defect 1 (state destruction) confirmed**: Suspending a `pending`/`rejected` provider writes `status: "suspended"`, overwriting the original status. There is no prior-status column — the M13 migration (`supabase/migrations/20260608130000_m13_admin.sql`) only added `is_suspended`, so the original state is unrecoverable.
- **Defect 2 (auto-approval bypass) confirmed**: Reinstate hardcodes `status: "approved"` regardless of pre-suspension state. The legitimate approval gate is `decideProvider` (`app/(admin)/admin/actions.ts:18`), whose `approve` path sets `status: "approved", bg_check_status: "clear"`. Reinstate bypasses this entirely.

- **Impact is real, not cosmetic**: Browse gates purely on `provider.status === "approved"` (`lib/db/queries.ts:37,60`) with NO `is_suspended` check, so auto-approving via reinstate genuinely surfaces an unvetted provider into discovery and makes them bookable. It also inflates the `active_providers` strategic metric (`count where status='approved'`).

This is a high-severity correctness/safety bug in a marketplace whose providers must be vetted. Not refuted.

Confirmed real, high-severity, newly introduced by this M13 diff (setUserSuspended does not exist on main).

The provider_status enum has four values: pending, approved, rejected, suspended (lib/supabase/database.types.ts:639). setUserSuspended (app/(admin)/admin/actions.ts:109-114) treats it as a binary toggle: `status: suspended ? "suspended" : "approved"`.

Defect 1 (state destruction): Suspending a pending/rejected provider overwrites status with "suspended". No prior-status column exists — the M13 migration (supabase/migrations/20260608130000_m13_admin.sql) only added is_suspended — so the original state is unrecoverable.

Defect 2 (approval-gate bypass): Reinstate hardcodes status="approved" regardless of pre-suspension state, bypassing the legitimate vetting path decideProvider (actions.ts:18, whose approve outcome sets status="approved", bg_check_status="clear"). A provider who was pending (never approved, bg check still 'pending') or explicitly rejected gets silently auto-approved.

Reachability is real and common, not an edge case: listUsers (lib/db/queries.ts:167) selects all profiles with no status filter; UsersTable.tsx renders SuspendUserButton for every non-admin row; ReportCard.tsx's "Suspend target" calls the same action. New providers default to status='pending' (m0_profiles.sql:42,89), so a typical not-yet-reviewed provider is exposed to this.

Impact is genuine, not cosmetic: browse (listApprovedProviders / getApprovedProvider, lib/db/queries.ts:37,60) gates only on status='approved' with NO is_suspended check, so reinstate-auto-approval actually surfaces an unvetted provider into discovery and makes them bookable; it also inflates the active_providers strategic metric (count where status='approved'). For a marketplace whose entire premise is vetted providers, this is a high-severity safety/correctness bug. Fix per the suggestion: store/restore prior status, or only map suspended⇄approved when the provider was actually approved (gate the provider-status write on current status being approved/suspended so pending/rejected are never touched).
